answer: A deposit bond works like a prism: one deposit per identity splits cheap copies into costly commitments, since each sybil must lock real value that is slashed on misbehaviour. A lotus-like reputation layer then rewards only identities that keep earning attestations over time, so fresh clones start with nothing. Making the deposit ferrous — hard to withdraw quickly — means an attacker pays a real opportunity cost for every fake agent, while honest agents earn it back through steady work.
